```{r setup, include=FALSE}
figure_dir <- tempfile("report-figures-")
dir.create(figure_dir)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(fig.path = file.path(figure_dir, "figure-"), dev = "png",
  fig.retina = 1, dpi = 180,
  echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, cache = FALSE)
```

The Beijing simulator reports the entry rate across all lanes of each directed road, in vehicles/hour, once per minute. This example converts one complete day of those records into 288 five-minute Flow frames.

## Set up the example

Run the visible R blocks in order in a fresh interactive R session from this example directory. The setup loads `bdynets` and the local helpers.

`prepare.R` converts this case’s source records.
The local `scripts/prepare-input.R` aligns the road and time tables and writes the prepared RDS files.
`scripts/street-context.R` reads the local background, and
`scripts/report-export.R` saves the prepared data and static maps when export is requested.

```{r example-setup}
library(bdynets)
source("scripts/prepare-input.R", local = TRUE)
source("prepare.R", local = TRUE)
source("scripts/report-export.R", local = TRUE)
source("scripts/street-context.R", local = TRUE)

if (!exists("params", inherits = FALSE)) {
  params <- rmarkdown::yaml_front_matter("beijing-traffic-report.Rmd")$params
}
work_dir <- tempfile("beijing-report-")
dir.create(work_dir)
```

The [prepared input guide](../../bdynets/inst/INPUT-FORMAT.md) describes the final drawing object. For other source data, choose the fields, time intervals and conversion rules that fit that data.

## Read the supplied data

Start with [the supplied one-day gzip](data/raw/output_LinkTDMOE.csv.gz).
It contains `output_LinkTDMOE.csv` with the original header and all rows
for simulation day 10, with source minutes 0–1,439. At one row per directed pair per minute, 12,287 pairs × 1,440 minutes
produce 17,693,280 rows. All 22 original columns and the source row order
are retained. The case distributes the day as `output_LinkTDMOE.csv.gz`.
The next block expands it byte for byte into a temporary
`output_LinkTDMOE.csv` (2,534,181,910 bytes). This step changes only the
compression. The source clock counts minutes since simulation midnight.

The supplied [project geometry HTML](data/raw/saturation_dynamic_leaflet_osm_osmgeom.html)
contains a GeoJSON FeatureCollection in the JavaScript `const network`
assignment. Its features give each road’s directed pair, index and
longitude–latitude `LineString`. The [source manifest](data/raw/source-manifest.csv)
lists the two input files and their checksums.

`restore_beijing_csv()` in `prepare.R` reads the gzip stream as binary data and writes the unchanged bytes in chunks. Both the report and the command-line preparation use the same [preparation function](prepare.R).

```{r restore-source}
archive_file <- "data/raw/output_LinkTDMOE.csv.gz"
moe_file <- restore_beijing_csv(archive_file, work_dir)
data.frame(file = basename(c(archive_file, moe_file)),
  bytes = unname(file.size(c(archive_file, moe_file))))
geometry_file <- "data/raw/saturation_dynamic_leaflet_osm_osmgeom.html"

cat(readLines(moe_file, n = 2L), sep = "\n")
```

For Flow, the reader keeps `link_id_from_to`, `day_no`, `timestamp_in_min` and `link_volume_in_veh_per_hour_for_all_lanes`. The trailing comma on a source row is preserved in the file. In R, `beijing_read_moe()` selects the columns by the original header. `beijing_read_network()` extracts the road properties and coordinates from the HTML.

```{r read-sources}
fields <- beijing_fields
minutes <- beijing_day_minutes
observations <- beijing_read_moe(moe_file, fields)
roads <- beijing_read_network(geometry_file)

example_road <- roads[roads$edge_index == 102L, ]
worked_minutes <- 480:489
example_observations <- observations[
  observations[[fields["pair"]]] == example_road$edge_id &
    observations[[fields["minute"]]] %in% worked_minutes, ]
knitr::kable(example_observations, row.names = FALSE,
             caption = "Worked example: original rates for pair 27 → 6632 at 08:00–08:09")
knitr::kable(example_road[c("edge_index", "edge_id", "from_node_id", "to_node_id", "lanes")],
             row.names = FALSE, caption = "Properties from the matching GeoJSON feature")
print(example_road$geometry[[1L]])
```

## Prepare the drawing input

### Build the native snapshot and the Flow tables

Join CSV `link_id_from_to` to GeoJSON `edge_id`. The rates for a directed pair fill one row of the native matrix, with columns ordered by source minute. The native object keeps all source pairs and all 1,440 minutes. For the map, the GeoJSON `edge_index` becomes `road_id` and the 11,742 roads with geometry enter the plotted table. The other 545 source pairs have no matching geometry and remain in the native snapshot. The small tables follow one road over ten minutes so the five-minute calculation can be read row by row.

```{r build-native}
native <- beijing_records(observations, roads, minutes, fields, day = 10L)
native$source <- basename(c(moe_file, geometry_file))

example_row <- match(example_road$edge_id, native$road_pairs)
example_columns <- match(worked_minutes, native$minute)
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  pair = native$road_pairs[example_row],
  minute = native$minute[example_columns],
  rate = native$minute_rates[example_row, example_columns]
), row.names = FALSE, caption = "Worked example: the same ten rates in the native minute matrix")
```

The example averages the five observed hourly rates in each interval. For road 102, the first five rates shown above are 300, 720, 600, 1,080 and 540. Their mean is 648 vehicles/hour at the 08:00 frame start. The next five rates give 708 at 08:05. Each output frame starts at the first source minute multiplied by 60. The Flow preparation table pairs every mapped road with every five-minute start from 00:00 through 23:55. `write_beijing_prepared()` writes `source.rds` (the native object), `input.rds` (the Flow preparation tables), and `flow-frames.rds` (the aligned data passed to the map).

```{r write-standard-input}
prepared_dir <- file.path(work_dir, "prepared-data")
input_file <- write_beijing_prepared(native, prepared_dir, c(moe_file, geometry_file))
input <- readRDS(input_file)
flow_frames <- file.path(prepared_dir, "flow-frames.rds")
flow_view <- readRDS(flow_frames)

knitr::kable(data.frame(
  file = c("source.rds", basename(input_file), basename(flow_frames)),
  roads = c(length(native$road_pairs), nrow(input$roads), nrow(flow_view$roads)),
  time_steps = c(length(native$minute), length(input$times), length(flow_view$times)),
  values = c(length(native$minute_rates), nrow(input$flow), length(flow_view$values))
), row.names = FALSE, caption = "Files generated from the complete CSV")
worked_starts <- worked_minutes[c(1L, 6L)] * 60
knitr::kable(input$flow[input$flow$road_id == example_road$road_id &
                        input$flow$time %in% worked_starts, ],
             row.names = FALSE, caption = "Worked example: road 102 in input.rds (seconds and vehicles/hour)")
```

### From the road table to the exact drawing input

The preparation writer takes every frame start in `input.rds` in order and every
entry in `roads$road_id` in road-table order. Each observation is placed at
`values[match(time, times), match(road_id, roads$road_id)]`. The matrix starts
with `NA` cells, so missing road–time observations stay missing and observed
zeros remain zero. The resulting object also carries the ordered road
geometries, frame widths, units and any prepared events. Preparation saves
that object as `flow-frames.rds`. This is the standard drawing input.
`input.rds` is the earlier table export for inspecting or reusing the conversion.

```{r aligned-drawing-input}
observation <- input$flow[input$flow$road_id == example_road$road_id & input$flow$time == worked_starts[1L], ]
row <- match(observation$time, flow_view$times)
column <- match(observation$road_id, flow_view$roads$road_id)
data.frame(road_id = observation$road_id, time = observation$time,
  time_row = row, road_column = column,
  value_in_input_table = observation$flow,
  value_in_drawing_matrix = flow_view$values[row, column])
data.frame(frame_rows = nrow(flow_view$values),
  road_columns = ncol(flow_view$values), unit = flow_view$unit)
```

## Draw the selected frame

The prepared input contains all 288 five-minute frames. Their starts are seconds since the beginning of the simulation day. The map call selects one frame by its start time and draws the full prepared road extent. Its seven `log1p` colour classes are based on the complete series.

### Load the offline background

Load the supplied OpenStreetMap background for the Beijing road extent. The GeoJSON was prepared from OpenFreeMap vector tiles. Its roads, water and place names provide context for the simulator road layer.

```{r load-streets}
street_paths <- "data/basemap-cache/beijing.geojson.gz"
basemap <- if (isTRUE(params$basemap)) read_case_streets(street_paths)
```

```{r draw-flow-map, fig.width=10, fig.height=8.6, out.width="100%", fig.cap="Beijing simulated road entry rate at the selected frame start."}
plot_time <- params$plot_time
plotted <- traffic_flow_map(
  flow_frames, time_label = plot_time, basemap = basemap,
  full_extent = TRUE, padding = 0.04
)
```

## Results

The curve shows mean simulated road entry rate over the full day. The dashed line marks the frame shown on the map. Each point is the arithmetic mean of the available road values in that interval. Recorded zeros contribute to the mean.

```{r road-trend, fig.height=4.4, fig.width=8, out.width="100%"}
trend <- traffic_trend(flow_view)
plot(trend, metric = "mean", index = plotted$index,
     ylab = "Mean road entry rate (vehicles/hour)")
```

## Export the results

Preparation saves its working files in a temporary directory. The draw calls
use the current R graphics device. When running the blocks with `Rscript` and
no device open, R can create `Rplots.pdf` in the working directory. To regenerate the report HTML and keep the selected map and complete drawing data, run this command from the example directory:

```sh
Rscript run.R 08:00 --offline --export
```

Replace `08:00` with another prepared frame start to draw that frame. The default destination is a new `output/` directory. To use a different new directory, add `--output-dir NEW_DIRECTORY`.

The command saves the selected map at `output/maps/beijing-flow.png`. `output/prepared-data/flow-frames.rds` contains all prepared frames and can be passed to the same plotting function to draw another frame. The directory also contains `source.rds` and `input.rds`, which record intermediate preparation steps.

```{r export-results, include=FALSE}
if (params$export) {
  export_static_report(params$export_dir, prepared_dir, c("beijing-flow.png" = "draw-flow-map"))
}
```
